brief.text:
Payments Reliability Operations is the engineering reliability and incident record for Stencil's fintech money-movement stack, centered on the ACH pipeline and the Pillar Bank relationship. The foundational event is the April 6 ACH pipeline failure, whose postmortem explains why money movement is held to a different engineering bar and which triggered the migration of ACH origination and return processing off Rails/Sidekiq workers onto the Go ach-originator service (ADR-024, using an outbox pattern). The cut-over slipped from June, then again to Aug 18 after a failed load test (reported at the Aug 17 mid-quarter check-in, which also kept KYC migration on track and moved the investing beta to early September as a 5% MTU beta pending Pillar sign-off). The retro credited a smooth cut-over, the shadow diff catching the only real bug (an R03 returns mapping error), the June slip paying off, and Sarah ramping quickly, while flagging dashboard lag, a noisy NACHA-cutoff alert, and unsustainable load on Marcus Bell. The ACH originator runbook defines first-five-minutes SEV1 triage when no file has been submitted for the current window: acknowledge the page, check the dashboard, post in the incident channel, then check leader election (advisory lock), stuck pending entries (SQS relay), and stuck packaged entries (SFTP submission).

The second anchor is the Sep 26 SEV1 duplicate round-up debit incident, caused by the legacy Rails/Sidekiq round-up sweep job, which led to ADR-031/032 and the push for idempotency keys on all money-moving jobs. The incident process uses a severity model and six phases (detect, triage, contain, eradicate, notify, review), with a notification obligations table covering Pillar Bank, DriveWealth, customers, regulators, the board, and the cyber insurer. A 2026-10-02 amendment states that Pillar's 24-hour notification rule explicitly covers operational incidents affecting customer funds, as the Sep 26 duplicates did. Related reliability work includes a Plaid near-miss: an access token refresh bug, live about four months, left old tokens valid in roughly 0.3% of refreshes. It had no impact but was classed as a 'loaded gun' P0 risk if Plaid enforced one token per user. Marcus Bell found it and CTO Maya Chen reviewed it. The push notification architecture splits transactional (Branch) and marketing (Customer.io) providers behind a thin Go abstraction routing by template_key, with limits of 3 marketing pushes per day, transactional debounce, quiet hours, and a global opt-out. Marcus's team estimates about 6 weeks to build it.

Governance and outward communication sit alongside this work: Pillar ACH ops reviews (mid-quarter check-in, Eng Staff, September Pillar MBR, Q3 QBR), board deck engineering sections, a SOC 2 status letter from Maya Chen, and diligence prep for the Elena Sorensen call. That prep covers scale headroom (151k MAU, with the Postgres primary the first component to break at 10x), the April 6 and Sep 26 incidents, investing beta position reconciliation drift, SOC 2 Type II readiness gaps, and key-person and VP Eng search risk. Q4 commitments assign owners and October 2026 deadlines for the position reconciliation fix, Android parity for investing screens, go/no-go #2, deleting the Sidekiq ACH code, NACHA-cutoff alert tuning, idempotency keys for money-moving jobs, and locking the Q4 plan. Open attention items concern PR review discipline for money-movement code: linking PRs to the ADRs or customer issues they implement, pass / fail / pass-with-conditions review decisions, and resisting author pressure such as 'I need to merge this today.' Typical questions here include what caused the duplicate debits, who must be notified within 24 hours, how to triage a missed ACH window, why the cut-over slipped, and what Q4 reliability work remains.
